title: Felix and the Provision
premise: Jonah Brightwater has spent nine years running her riverboat, the Provision, up and down the Vell, outrunning debts, memories, and the oath that keeps every captain off the upper river, where the water is said to remember what it's given. When her old rival Sable Corvane offers a fortune to haul a sealed cargo to the source, Jonah refuses — until Sable's agents take her young deckhand Felix hostage as insurance. Dragged upstream through drowned towns, hostile locks, and a river that seems to push back, Jonah discovers the cargo is the Vell's stolen heart, and that Felix's family were the river's last sworn keepers. In the end Jonah chooses loyalty over survival, returning the heart to the source at the cost of the Provision and nearly her life, and finds that belonging was never a place she could run to — it was a promise she finally keeps.
about_author: J. M. Almeida is a former barge mechanic who spent a decade working the inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who love places that refuse to love them back.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A routine run down the lower Vell establishes Jonah's restless expertise and her bond with Felix, the orphaned deckhand she took in. When a dockmaster mentions traffic on the forbidden upper river, Jonah shuts the conversation down hard. Beat: comfort shadowed by old fear.

chapters.title: A Debt with Teeth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix explores a river town while the Provision takes on cargo and finds a wanted poster bearing Jonah's face — and a second poster offering reward for 'keepers of the source.' He pockets it, uneasy. Beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Woman from Before
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sable Corvane boards at nightfall with a contract: one sealed cargo, one trip to the source, triple pay. Jonah throws her off the boat, but Sable's parting words — she knows what Jonah buried at the source nine years ago — land like a hook. Beat: defiance masking terror.

chapters.title: What Felix Saw
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix wakes to shouting: Sable's agents have boarded, taken the cargo manifest, and left a message — deliver the shipment or Felix answers for it. Jonah realizes the threat was never about money. Beat: violation and helpless rage.

chapters.title: Crew of the Willing
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah gathers her skeleton crew — engineer Bramm, cook Odile — and tells them the truth for the first time. Two walk, three stay. The choice to go upstream, breaking the captains' oath, splits her loyalty between her crew and her word. Beat: costly commitment.

chapters.title: The Last Lock
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Provision passes the final manned lock before forbidden water; the lockkeeper, an old friend of Jonah's, begs her to turn back and reveals Sable has bought every lock ahead. Beat: the point of no passage back.

chapters.title: Drowned Bellhaven
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They navigate a town deliberately flooded decades ago, its rooftops just under the surface. Jonah recognizes the flood as no accident — the source was dammed to hide something. Bramm finds sabotage marks on the hull overnight. Beat: creeping revelation.

chapters.title: Passenger in the Hold
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix investigates the sealed cargo and finds a living stowaway: a gaunt old man, Wren, who claims to be the last keeper of the source and says the cargo is a cage. Sable's agents are hunting Wren too. Beat: the mission's true shape emerges.

chapters.title: The Oathbreakers' Reach
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Sable's gunboat corners them in a narrows; Jonah wins escape by a reckless run through rapids no captain would attempt, but Odile is badly hurt. The river saved them — or tested them. Beat: triumph priced in blood.

chapters.title: What Jonah Buried
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Wren coaxes the truth from Jonah: nine years ago she helped steal the river's heart — the source-stone — believing she was freeing the valley from the keepers' control. The floods and dying fish began that season. Beat: guilt finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Felix's Name
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah confronts Felix with the poster: his family were keepers, and Sable has known all along — Felix was the insurance and the bait both. Felix feels used; Jonah feels seen through. Their bond fractures. Beat: betrayal inside loyalty.

chapters.title: The Corvane Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Wren deciphers Sable's plan: the heart doesn't grant power, it grants claim — whoever holds it owns every mile of the Vell, its towns, its tolls. Sable doesn't want to free the river; she wants to own it. Beat: the stakes turn civic and vast.

chapters.title: Mutiny Weather
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A storm forces them to ground the Provision; Bramm, terrified, argues for dumping the cargo and running. Jonah, for the first time, agrees with the oath instead of her crew — and is outvoted. Beat: leadership inverted; humility learned.

chapters.title: The Toll of Ashport
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the last town before the source, they find Sable has already arrived, buying loyalty with bread and promises. Felix, using his keeper's face, walks into her camp as a spy and learns where she'll take the cage. Beat: courage through deception.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Felix is caught. Sable offers Jonah the trade she always intended: the heart for the boy, delivered to the source, where Sable will install herself as the river's owner with Jonah's hands doing the work. Beat: the trap fully sprung.

chapters.title: The Long Haul
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Under guard, the Provision climbs the final reach — water growing strangely clear, strangely awake, pulling the boat like it knows the way home. Wren whispers that the river isn't dragging them to doom; it's dragging them to judgment. Beat: dread and awe entwined.

chapters.title: The Source of the Vell
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They arrive at a spring-fed amphitheater of stone where the river is born. Sable forces Jonah to open the cage. The heart, freed, does not obey her — the river rises to take back what was stolen, and it begins with Sable's claim. Beat: power meeting its corruption.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Choice
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The heart will return to the source only if carried by a keeper's hand — and Felix's blood is thin keeper's blood. Jonah refuses to let the boy pay for her sin and takes the stone herself, knowing it may burn out her life. Beat: loyalty answering truth.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah wades into the source with the heart; the river shows her every consequence of the theft — the drowned town, the dying fish — then, weighing her return against her theft, spares her but claims the Provision, dragging the boat down as payment. Beat: judgment and mercy.

chapters.title: After the Flood
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The river runs clean again; Sable's claim dissolves and her hired guns melt away. The crew stands on the bank with nothing but each other, watching the Provision's mast sink. Odile laughs first. Beat: grief braided with release.

chapters.title: The Keeping
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The valley towns, freed from Sable's tolls, ask Wren and Felix to restore the keepers — but as stewards, not owners. Jonah, offered a captaincy ashore, chooses instead to help build a new boat. Beat: belonging finally accepted, on honest terms.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, closing on Jonah. Months later, a new keel takes the water, named Provision. Felix at the wheel, Jonah at the rail, the river easy beneath them for the first time in nine years. Stopping no longer costs more than running. Beat: homecoming without arrival — just peace, held.
